scope: Exact Haar-preserving raw-kernel symmetries preserve the already constructed original full positive ground, stationary squared mass, raw transition and variance loss. Actual spatial translations and all coordinate permutations satisfy these hypotheses; reversed plaquette orientations are handled by the inverse-character identity. A constructed relocation takes the canonical crossing plaquette to every spatial location and orientation on an even-period lattice. Consequently the supported-source decay M(PF)<=cap(beta)^2*exp(-beta*R)*M(F) holds at every spatial plaquette for beta>=3/4. Gauge-invariant continuous square cutoffs give arbitrary finite families one joint source localization: integral_B F^2 dpi<=2*loss(F)+2*delta*M(F), where B is the union of D_p>=2R_p and delta=sum_p cap(beta)^2*exp(-beta*R_p). The one-step output tail is <=delta*M(F). A new reverse cutoff-duality argument proves the sharper supported-union bound M(PF)<=delta*M(F), hence loss(F)>=(1-delta)*M(F), for every continuous source supported in B. No separation, independence or source-factorization premise is used. For all plaquettes delta=3*(2n)^3*cap(beta)^2*exp(-beta*R). The exact entropy condition log(3*(2n)^3*cap(beta)^2)+t<=beta*R implies delta<=exp(-t). The limitation of this bound is also proved: if 2*beta<=3*log(2n) and R<=2, then delta>=3; if R>2 the hard event is empty. This is a limitation of the all-plaquette estimate, not a no-go theorem about the actual law or mass gap. For any fixed finite family, the threshold R=4*log(beta)/beta vanishes and its exact rate is C/beta, C=(4*SU2ScalarTilt.partition(0)/Gamma(3/2))^2. Bounded-mass approximate slow sources therefore concentrate below this threshold on every fixed finite family, uniformly in moving locations and arbitrary changing even periods. The law is the actual original full-ground law; raw/full agreement on the physical sector remains the established one. Retained-region global coercivity, actual distant mixed-ground or signed-form control, a compatible physical trajectory and nonzero continuum survival remain open; all twelve Clay requirements remain open.
